title.en: Finite-window FFT spectrum and inverse reconstruction

summary: Compare one finite sampled signal under rectangular and tapered windows, reconstruct the exact windowed samples by inverse DFT, and distinguish bin spacing from true frequency resolution.
objective: Make leakage, window response, coherent scaling and exact finite inverse reconstruction visible without presenting zero padding as new measured information.
intent_signals: Show why an off-bin sinusoid leaks across FFT bins and reconstruct the windowed samples exactly.
Compare rectangular and Hann windows with zero padding but keep the original record length visible.
example_prompts: Show why an off-bin sinusoid leaks across FFT bins and reconstruct the windowed samples exactly.
Compare rectangular and Hann windows with zero padding but keep the original record length visible.
negative_signals: Not a continuous Fourier-series harmonic editor.
Not proof of frequencies between samples or beyond Nyquist.
not_for: Irregular samples, streaming STFT or statistical PSD confidence intervals.
Recovering the unwindowed signal after a window with zeros from windowed samples alone.

entities.name: Finite sample rail
entities.guidance: Show n=64..2048 real samples x_m at t_m=m*dt, the window w_m and product y_m=x_m w_m with the same stable index.

entities.name: Linked complex spectrum
entities.guidance: Plot signed frequency bins f_k and complex Y_k, plus magnitude/phase; selected bin links its contribution to every reconstructed sample. Phase is unavailable when magnitude is zero or below the declared phase threshold.

entities.name: Inverse reconstruction rail
entities.guidance: Compute yhat_m=(1/n) sum_k Y_k exp(2 pi i mk/n) under the declared convention and show max complex residual.

state_contract.model: Require finite dt>0, integer 64<=n<=2048 and finite real x_m. Choose rectangular w_m=1 or periodic Hann w_m=0.5(1-cos(2 pi m/n)); report coherent gain CG=sum_m w_m/n. Compute y_m=x_m w_m and Y_k=sum_m y_m exp(-2 pi i mk/n). Optional zero padding changes transform length nfft>=n but never the original n or record duration. Inverse reconstruction uses the same full complex n-point Y when checking y.
state_contract.authority: Numeric arrays, dt, window, transform length and normalization own every coordinate; mesh height and color are display only.
actions: Choose on-bin or off-bin sinusoid preset and add bounded second component.
Switch window and recompute spectrum, coherent gain readout and inverse.
Change zero-padding factor while pinning n and dt.
Select a bin or sample; play/scrub contribution assembly; reset exactly.

invariants: For x_m=cos(2 pi*8m/n), rectangular-window energy is confined to conjugate bins 8 and n-8 within numerical tolerance.
For an off-bin sinusoid, nonzero neighboring bins are labeled finite-window leakage, not extra physical tones.
Full forward then inverse DFT reconstructs y_m, not generally x_m; report max |yhat-y| and imaginary residue.
Zero padding makes a denser sampled spectrum but does not change duration n*dt or acquired samples.
Reject nonfinite input, nfft<n and inverse residual above declared tolerance.
motion_guidance: Scrub integer samples or bins; interpolation is explanatory.
When window or n changes, invalidate spectrum and reconstruction atomically.
creative_affordances: Use a braided phasor ring, translucent bin columns or engraved sample rail while preserving signed frequency and non-color window cues.
known_limits: A finite record cannot establish a unique continuous spectrum or sub-bin tone without assumptions.
Window choice trades main-lobe width and sidelobes; no window is universally best. No computation was run.

claims.statement: NumPy defines the forward DFT as A_k=sum from m=0 to n-1 of a_m exp(-2 pi i m k/n) and its inverse with 1/n and the opposite sign.
claims.scope: NumPy 2.2 documented convention; other libraries and normalization modes may differ.

source_refs.locator: Implementation details, forward and inverse DFT equations

claims.statement: The SciPy spectral-analysis guide attributes sidelobe leakage for a finite-duration sine to confinement to a finite interval and describes windowing as suppressing secondary lobes at the cost of widening the main lobe.
claims.scope: Finite sampled spectral analysis in the cited guide; it does not identify a universal optimal window.

source_refs.locator: Spectral Analysis, finite sine leakage and windowed DFT equation (7)

object_craft.structure: Place sample/window/product rails below a signed-frequency spectrum and a separate reconstruction rail; keep zero padding as denser thin bin marks, not more input samples.
object_craft.material: Use one neutral window envelope, distinct magnitude and phase encodings, and hatch unresolved or thresholded values.
object_craft.articulation: A selected bin fans contribution curves to reconstruction samples; window tokens swap the numeric input atomically.

object_craft.structure: In Blender, author only static axes, labeled frames, selection glyphs and low-detail instrument housings at declared units; keep numeric curves, rasters, samples and component lattices out of baked mesh state.
object_craft.material: Use simple glTF-safe material slots and optional baked label atlases with explicit UVs. Export named anchors and static teaching geometry; unsupported procedural nodes, text and compositor marks require baked or runtime replacements.
object_craft.articulation: In Three.js, allocate numeric arrays from the validated input contract, generate dynamic lines/points/instances, bind selections by stable index, and rebuild all linked views atomically on parameter revision or reset.

physical_contract.scope: Finite complex DFT of a windowed sample vector; no physical signal model.
physical_contract.timestep: One integer sample or bin index per explanatory step; no continuous dynamics.
checks: Confirm padding leaves n and duration unchanged.
